newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, with gains powered by expected tight hog supplies, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.

Tight supplies were partly expected to come from reluctance among some farmers to ship hogs if temperatures and humidity remain high, sources said. Temperatures were expected to reach the 90s across the Midwest Monday and in the eastern Corn Belt on Tuesday, with somewhat cooler readings Wednesday in the western belt but continued warm east, Weather Services Corporation said near midday.

Extreme heat and humidity can slow weight gains and stress hogs during shipping, but the recent heat has not been around long enough to do any lasting damage, said Dave Maher, livestock analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.
"The numbers are down because the hogs just aren't there," Maher said.
Slow expansion late last year kept hog supplies tight, Maher added. Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs were seen steady, with a top of $60.00 for hogs delivered to the plant.
Illinois top prices for hogs at the plant were seen $60.00 to $60.50. Indiana/Ohio top hog values at the plant were expected at $60.00, livestock dealers said.
